endorsements.title: Marketing Submission Recommendations for a Predetermined Change Control Plan for AI-Enabled Device Software Functions (final guidance)
endorsements.quote: you will need to submit a new marketing submission that includes the device that you would like to introduce a PCCP for, as well as the PCCP that you are proposing in that new submission

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions: Lifecycle Management and Marketing Submission Recommendations (draft guidance)
endorsements.quote: In situations where manufacturers wish to consider development of models that automatically or continuously update, FDA encourages manufacturers to use the Q-S ubmission Program to discuss considerations related to these AI models early in the development process and review the FDA guidance titled “Marketing Submission Recommendations for a Predetermined Change Control Plan for Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions.”

endorsements.title: Considerations for the regulation of generative AI-enabled medical devices (discussion paper)
endorsements.quote: A Predetermined Change Control Plan (PCCP)22 could be one mechanism to facilitate certain device changes without requiring a new premarket submission.

commentary.bottom_line: Three FDA documents support submitting a predetermined change control plan through a marketing submission and obtaining authorization before relying on it, with the final guidance stating this as a requirement. No study has tested whether this practice reduces unreviewed model modifications or patient harm, and no study documents how often the targeted hazard occurs.

perspectives.view: No study tests the practice, and no study documents the hazard it targets. The recommendation rests entirely on regulatory guidance and a discussion paper. Under GRADE conventions, certainty about any effect on unauthorized model changes or patient outcomes cannot be rated, so the evidence base is best described as absent.

The final PCCP guidance states that manufacturers need a new marketing submission containing the plan, which makes authorization a precondition rather than an option. The draft lifecycle guidance encourages early Q-Submission discussion for continuously updating models. The generative AI discussion paper describes the plan as one possible mechanism, which suggests its scope for generative models remains unsettled.

commentary.research_gap: No study measures how often manufacturers implement model changes under plans that FDA has not authorized, or whether the authorization requirement changes post-market performance, safety signals, or recall rates. Studies comparing devices modified under authorized plans with devices modified through new submissions would help establish whether the process affects patient outcomes.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested this practice in any population, so there is no evidence on Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy patients. Health systems cannot tell from current evidence whether authorized change control plans address performance shifts that may fall unevenly on these groups after a model is updated.
